verdict.reasoning: Patient states having a “blinding headache for a few days” and later clarifies “that was three days ago, and I just keep having it.”

Onset: “it just started all of a sudden. I woke up one morning with a headache, and that was three days ago.” Constant: “Kinda all the time.” Global and worse over right eye: “it's kind of all over but, I feel like over my right eye, it's… stronger.”
Severity and response: “I guess it's mostly, eight, and then it kinda comes down to maybe a five.” and “when I take Ibuprofen it gets a bit better… but then I still have it.”

Photophobia: “lights definitely make me more sensitive… I don't really, like strong lights.” Visual aura: “I get this, shooting light sometimes… weird kind of vision.” Mild nausea: “no, feeling a bit sick, but no vomiting.”
Positional/head movement triggering: “Sometimes when I stand up, quickly I get a bit of a, stabbing pain. Um, or if I throw my head like, it I kind of feel like something is moving inside.”
Not nocturnal but present on waking: “Um, yeah, I'm, sleeping well.” / “Is it waking you up in the night-time?” – “No, no, no. But I can wake up with it in the morning.”

No prior similar severe headaches but brief previous one responsive to ibuprofen: “Not really just they're, on and off… I recently had a, a one for like two days… but it just went away with Ibuprofen, so nothing like, more, longer than two days before.”

Fever: “you haven't had a high temperature. Have you checked your temperature?” – “I don't really feel, feverish or anything.” URTI/sinus: “have you had any cold symptoms, sore throat… pain over the sinuses? Any cough or flem?” – “No, no.” Neuro deficits: “Any tingling? Or numbness? Or weakness anywhere?” – “Um, no.” Smell/taste: “Any change in your smell or taste?” – “No, none at all.”

Past medical history: “any other, medical problems in the past?” Patient: “I think I only had a, a pain, um, when I was younger but, no causes found and that went away, but that's, the only thing I know of.” This supports no significant ongoing past medical conditions.

Medication: “Do you take any medications?” – “Um, just the pill.” Started 1 year ago: “And when did you start that?” – “Um, about a year ago.” Doctor’s later discussion indicates a combined pill (“that pill… we’d have to change it… particularly”), matching combined oral contraceptive.
Ibuprofen PRN: “apart from the Ibuprofen that I take, sometimes when, the headache gets really bad, nothing else.”
Allergies: “Um, and any allergies to anything?” – “No.”
Family history: “my mum, suffers from, like she has migraines… she has quite bad migraines, she's like, has the vomiting and everything.”
Living situation: “Who do you live with at home?” – “Uh, just by myself.” Work from home: “Have you been at work recently?” – “Um, I work from home…”

Misses work due to headaches: “couldn't really manage to, do it all the time. So sometimes I just took a day off… the second I just took the whole day off… I couldn't focus.” Non-smoker: “And do you smoke?” – “Uh, no.”
Alcohol use: “Do you drink any alcohol regularly?” – “Yeah.” / “How much in a normal week?” – “Um, probably like, three , once a week.” This supports ~3 drinks once weekly.
Drug use: “And do you take any other drugs at all?” – “Um, no apart from the Ibuprofen… nothing else.”

Assessment content: Doctor: “it… could possibly be a migraine type headache. But, the fact it's still ongoing for three days, we probably should, book you into an appointment to get an examination.” New severe headache for 3 days with visual aura-like symptoms (“shooting light sometimes”) supports ‘possible migraine with visual aura versus other secondary headaches’ as a clinical impression.

COCP use and BP check: patient on pill for a year; doctor: “Have you had your blood pressure checked recently with your pill?” … “when you have a, an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well. Just to, make sure your pill's still appropriate for you.”

COCP contraindication in migraine with aura: Doctor: “if we do think it's a migraine, then you would have to change your pill. If you've had these flashing lights, and things like that.” This reflects considering COCP contraindication if migraine with aura is confirmed.
Suboptimal pain control: “Doesn't really go away with Ibuprofen… It gets a little bit better but like, doesn't go away.” and “when I take Ibuprofen it gets a bit better… but then I still have it.”

Face-to-face exam, neuro, fundoscopy, BP: “we probably should, book you into an appointment to get an examination… we should do a neurological examination, look at the back of your eyes as well.” and “when you have a, an examination with us, we'll check your blood pressure as well.” This implies an urgent in-person appointment.

Medication plan: “I can prescribe you something, similar to Ibuprofen, but a bit stronger which you can take instead of Ibuprofen. And you can also take Paracetamol at the same time… take it with food.” A stronger NSAID plus paracetamol with food is explicitly described.

A&E safety netting: “if in the meantime before your appointment your, headache is getting unbearable, getting worse or changing. Then, um, if it's that bad, then you should go to A and E and have an examination.” Earlier they discussed visual symptoms; this covers escalation/new concerning features such as worsening vision or neuro signs.
